newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dexia has right of refusal on rest of Crediop.
newsitem.headline: Dexia has right of refusal on rest of Crediop.

text.p: Credit Communal de Belgique (CCB), the Belgian arm of Belgian-French alliance Dexia, said on Monday Dexia had the right of first refusal on those shares in Italy's Crediop SpA it did not already own.
Earlier on Monday Dexia said it bought 40 percent in Crediop from Italy's San Paolo group.

"There are no options attached to the deal, but the Dexia group has the right of first refusal on the full 60 percent of Crediop still owned by San Paolo," CCB chief executive officer Francois Narmon told a news conference.
He said the 40 percent stake would be bought by and lodged in CCB and Credit Local de France, the operational arms of Dexia group. CLF is the French arm.
"The Crediop stake will lodged one half at CCB and one half at CLF. It is the operational banks taking the stakes, not the holding companies," he said.
Under their alliance the two banks have each created a holding company, which each has a 50 percent in the Belgian and French operational banks.
Narmon said that both banks will also split 50/50 the one percent stake they plan to buy in Crediop parent Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino in the second round of the privatisation of San Paolo.
The stake will cost 1.6-1.7 billion Belgian francs ($46.3-$49.2 million), he said.
Narmon said that neither CCB or CLF would issue new stock to fund the acquisition of 40 percent in Crediop. "It will be financed with our own means. We do not need a capital increase."
